newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus bourse suspends trading in cement companies.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus bourse suspends trading in cement companies.

text.p: Cyprus's bourse on Tuesday ordered a suspension of trading in shares of two cement companies amid confusing reports of a merger or takeover of one by the other.
The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) board suspended trading in the Vassiliko Cement Works and the Cyprus Cement Company until further notice.
"Reports in recent days caused some confusion and we want it cleared up," bourse director Nondas Metaxas told Reuters.
Italy's Italcementi owns 33 percent of Vassiliko and is the biggest shareholder. The Church-controlled Hellenic Mining Company (HMC) is the second largest.

A bull run started on the shares of Vassiliko and Cyprus Cement last week after the head of the Greek Orthodox Church of Cyprus, Archbishop Chrysostomos, told reporters the HMC was interested in selling about 30 percent of Vassiliko shares to the "Cypriot company", referring to Cyprus Cement.
Vassiliko fully paid shares gained 24 percent and Cyprus Cement 11.9 percent on what market players described as speculative buying last week. Monday was a market holiday.
But subsequent to the market suspension on Tuesday officials of both companies dismissed knowledge of purchase plans.

"The board of the exchange believes that more clarifications are needed (before trading resumes)," said Metaxas, implying that explanations were due not only from the two companies directly involved, but other "interested parties" as well.

The bourse ordered the temporary suspension of shares in both companies again last December after Cyprus Cement announced a deal to buy 47.5 percent of Vassiliko shares -- only to be scuppered when Vassiliko announced a deal with Italcementi instead. In January the Italian group upped its stake in the company to 33 percent from 20 percent it has held from 1990.
Italcementi issued a statement to brokers on Tuesday saying it was satisfied with maintaining its shareholding position at the current level.

"However in case of any attempt by a third party to buy Vassiliko shares controlled by the HMC we fully intend to exercise our pre-emption right on these shares in order to continue our cooperation in Vassiliko," said a statement signed by Italcementi representative Jean-Yves Gestin.
